gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up today.
gaps.explanation: 'Anyone who' is the standard pattern; 'who' is the subject pronoun for people.

gaps.sentence: The river ___ runs through the town often floods in spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject relative pronoun for things and animals.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: They chose a guide on ___ they could rely completely.
gaps.hint: rely on somebody — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: After the preposition 'on', the person takes 'whom'; 'which' is only for things.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: The exam, the results of ___ will be published on Friday, was very difficult.
gaps.hint: quantity noun + of + thing in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'The results of which' joins the clauses formally; 'of whom' is for people and 'of them' cannot link clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ my grandmother was born has no shops.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb for places; 'which' cannot stand alone here because no preposition is present.
